newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola, flax end lower, grains mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola, flax end lower, grains mostly lower.

text.p: WCE canola and flaxseed futures closed lower, pressured largely by a drop in CBOT soy complex futures Thursday, traders said.
Feed grains were mostly lower, weighed down by expected increases in hedge selling during the current warmer trend in the Prairie provinces.

In addition to the lower CBOT soybean complex, traders said light export demand encouraged selling in canola. Traders said Japan may have bought 1,000 to 2,000 tonnes of canola late Tuesday, but relatively high prices have discouraged large sales to Japan or other countries.
Canola closed down $3.30 to $2.50 with March off $3.20 at $406.00 per tonne.
Commercial selling was noted in flaxseed, which closed down $5.30 to $2.40 with March off $5.00 at $346.20.

Feed grains were lightly traded with traders featured moving long February barley positions to March. Barley closed down $0.70 to $1.60 with February off $1.00 at $137.70 and March was off $0.70 at $136.90.
Wheat was up $0.40 to off $0.40 with March up $0.40 at $170.60. Oats did not trade and February feed peas traded down $1.00 at $206.00
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except oats and peas.)
